title: 13 — Design a Search Autocomplete System
html:
13 — Design a Search Autocomplete System

The one idea: don't compute suggestions at query time. Build a trie offline from aggregated query logs, cache the top-k completions at every node, and serve them from memory. Lookups become O(1)-ish; freshness comes from rebuilding weekly (or streaming for trending terms).

Step 1 — Scope

  • Matching only at the beginning of a query (prefix match).
  • Return 5 suggestions, ordered by popularity (historical query frequency).
  • English, lowercase, no spell-check (for now).
  • 10M DAU; results within 100 ms (else the UI stutters).

Estimates

  • 10 searches/user/day × 20 chars each → one request per keystroke → 10M × 10 × 20 ÷ 10^5 ≈ ~24,000 QPS, peak ~48,000.
  • New data: ~20% of queries are new → ~0.4 GB/day added.

Step 2 — High-level design

Two services:

  • Data gathering: aggregates queries into a frequency table (query, frequency).
  • Query service: given a prefix, returns top 5 by frequency.

Naive query: SELECT * FROM frequency_table WHERE query LIKE 'pre%' ORDER BY frequency DESC LIMIT 5 — fine for small data, too slow at scale.

Step 3 — Deep dive

3.1 Trie

Each node = a prefix; children = next characters; nodes that end a query store its frequency.

Naive top-k: find the prefix node (O(p)), traverse the subtree to find all completions (O(c)), sort (O(c log c)) — too slow for short prefixes like "a".

Two optimisations:

  1. Limit prefix length (e.g. 50 chars) → finding the node is O(1).
  2. Cache top-k at every node → no subtree traversal. Costs memory, but it's the whole trick.
---
title: Trie with cached top-k per node
---
flowchart TB
    root(("root")) --> b(("b<br/>[be:35, bee:20, beer:10, best:35]"))
    b --> be(("be<br/>[best:35, bee:20, beer:10]"))
    be --> bee(("bee<br/>[bee:20, beer:10]"))
    be --> bes(("bes<br/>[best:35]"))
    bee --> beer(("beer:10"))
    bes --> best(("best:35"))

3.2 Data gathering service

Updating the trie on every query is too expensive, and top suggestions rarely change minute to minute.

---
title: Autocomplete — data gathering pipeline
---
flowchart LR
    L["Analytics logs<br/>(raw queries)"] --> A["Aggregators<br/>(weekly or daily)"]
    A --> AD[("Aggregated data<br/>query, time, freq")]
    AD --> W["Workers<br/>build trie"]
    W --> TDB[("Trie DB")]
    TDB --> TC[("Trie cache<br/>(in memory)")]
  • Trie DB options: serialised trie snapshots in a document store, or a KV store mapping prefix → top-k list (the trie flattened into a hash table — easy to shard).
  • Rebuild weekly for most use cases; real-time for trending (see wrap-up).

3.3 Query service

  • Client → LB → API → trie cache (miss → trie DB) → return.
  • AJAX requests so the page doesn't reload.
  • Browser caching: suggestions for a prefix barely change → Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600.
  • Data sampling: log only 1 in N queries to save processing.
  • Debounce keystrokes on the client (e.g. 100–150 ms).

3.4 Trie operations

Operation Approach
Create Built by workers from aggregated data
Update Replace the whole trie weekly, or update a node and its ancestors' top-k
Delete Filter layer in front of the cache removes hateful/violent/dangerous suggestions immediately; physically removed in the next rebuild

3.5 Scaling storage

Shard by first character → unbalanced ('s' ≫ 'x'). Better: a shard map manager that splits by historical load (e.g. s alone on one shard, u–z together on another).

Step 4 — Wrap-up

  • Multiple languages: store Unicode characters in trie nodes.
  • Per-country tries, served via CDN.
  • Trending / real-time queries: the weekly trie can't show breaking news. Use a streaming pipeline (Kafka → Flink/Spark) with time-decayed scores, weight recent queries more, and merge a small real-time trie with the big one.

.NET / Azure mapping

  • Azure AI Search has built-in suggesters (/suggest and /autocomplete APIs) with prefix matching and fuzzy options — the managed answer for product search.
  • Redis: store prefix → top-k as a sorted set per prefix (ZREVRANGE prefix:be 0 4); or use FT.SUGADD / FT.SUGGET (RediSearch).
  • Build job: an Azure Function or Container Apps job that aggregates logs (from Event Hubs → Data Lake) and writes the prefix table.
  • In-process: an immutable trie loaded into memory and swapped atomically (Interlocked.Exchange) on rebuild — no locks on the read path.
  • Angular client: debounceTime(150), distinctUntilChanged(), switchMap() to cancel stale requests.

Review checklist

  • Estimate QPS (per keystroke!).
  • Trie + top-k cached per node; prefix length capped.
  • Offline aggregation and rebuild; not on the request path.
  • Browser caching, debouncing, sampling.
  • Filter layer for unsafe suggestions.
  • Sharding by load, not alphabet; trending via streaming.
